data_source.title: Data source
data_source.description: Bluetooth works with no extra setup. MQTT delivers readings every 30 seconds and stops the Bluetooth polling that can disturb the pairing, but the device must already be provisioned to a broker you host: port 443, WebSocket over TLS, anonymous listener. No entities are added either way — the existing sensors just change what feeds them.

provision.title: Provision device
provision.description: Sends the WiFi network, and optionally a broker address, to the monitor over Bluetooth. It only advertises for a short window after losing a connection, so press the button on the device first. The broker address needs a six-character scheme prefix such as tcp:// which the device strips without reading; a hostname works as well as an address. The Bluetooth link is dropped at the end, which is when the device joins.

error.serial_required: A serial number is required for MQTT: it is the topic suffix.
error.provisioning_failed: Could not reach the device. Press its button to make it discoverable, then try again.
